case_name: Jagdish and another v State of Harayan
respondent:
State of Harayan
Supreme Court of India

17 December 2003
Cr.A. Nos. 432 of 1997
The Order of the Court was as follows :
1. The two appellants in this appeal and one Karambir were charged for the offences punishable u/s. 302 read with 34 IPC and S. 325 read with 34 IPC before the Court of Sessions Judge, Faridabad for having committed the murder of one Jabar Khan and for having caused grievous injuries to one Prem Chand, PW.9. Learned Sessions Judge after trial came to the conclusion that the prosecution has established its case against the said accused persons accordingly it sentenced the three accused including two appellants herein to imprisonment for life for an offence punishable u/s. 302 read with 34 IPC and a further sentenced them to rigorous imprisonment for three years and a fine of Rs.1,000/- each for an offence punishable under S. 325 read with 34. He directed that the said sentences shall run concurrently and further directed that in the event of fine
facts: The two appellants and one Karambir were charged for the offences punishable u/s. 302 read with 34 IPC and S. 325 read with 34 IPC before the Court of Sessions Judge, Faridabad.
There was dispute between Udham Singh and Jagdish on the one side and the complainant, PW.9 Prem Chand the injured witness on the other in regard to certain land.

On 14th September, 1990 at about 10 a.m. when the said Prem Chand (PW.9) and his son, Dev Dutt(PW.8) were harvesting jawar crops standing in their land three accused persons armed with farsa and axe came to their land and attacked Prem Chand, PW.9.
A complaint in this regard was lodged by PW.8, Dev Dutt in Hassanpur Police Station.
After investigation a chargesheet was filed and as stated above and the two courts below have convicted the appellants.
issues: Whether the prosecution has established its case against the said accused persons
Whether the courts below committed error in coming to the conclusion that the appellants before us are not guilty of the offences charged against them
petitioner_arguments: According to the prosecution that the incident in question occurred in the land of the appellants themselves but from the prosecution evidence there was no blood stain found in the said land.
The FIR/complaint was lodged after due deliberation.
court_reasoning: We have heard learned counsel and perused the record. From the perusal of the evidence of Pws.8, 9 and 10, we have no reason to conclude either of the courts below committed error in coming to the conclusion that the appellants before us are not guilty of the offences charged against them.

The courts below had noticed this fact and had relied upon the evidence of PW.12, the Investigating Officer who had stated that he had found blood stains from the place of incident in which the deceased was done to death hence rejected the said argument.
holding: For the reasons stated above, the appeal fails and the same is dismissed.
